## Multiple Comparisons (Tukey) {#sec-tukey}

```{r}
#| label: setup-4-2
#| include: false
source(if (file.exists("R/setup.R")) "R/setup.R" else "../R/setup.R")
crd <- read.csv(data_path("pricing_crd.csv"))
crd$strategy <- factor(crd$strategy, levels = c("Regular", "Discount", "Bundle"))
sav <- read.csv(data_path("saving_rate.csv"))
sav$region <- factor(sav$region, levels = c("North", "Northeast", "Central", "South"))
sales <- crd$sales; strategy <- crd$strategy
saving <- sav$saving; region <- sav$region
model <- aov(sales ~ strategy)
model_sav <- aov(saving ~ region)
```

### Learning Objectives

1. Explain when a multiple-comparison procedure is needed.
2. Read the output of `TukeyHSD()`: difference, confidence interval and adjusted p-value.
3. Decide which pairs of means differ and write the conclusion.

### Concept

When ANOVA rejects $H_0$, we know that **at least one** mean is different, but
not which ones. Comparing every pair with separate $t$ tests would raise the
overall chance of a Type I error, as Section 4.1 explained.

**Tukey's honestly significant difference (HSD)** method compares every pair
of means while keeping the **family-wise** error rate (the chance of at least
one Type I error among all the comparisons) at $\alpha$ = 0.05. It is based on
the Studentized range distribution (Table 14). In this course we read Tukey's
results from R only.

::: {.callout-important icon=false}
## When to use Tukey

Use Tukey only **after** the ANOVA $F$ test rejects $H_0$. If ANOVA accepts
$H_0$, the conclusion is that all the means are equal, and no pairwise
comparison is needed.
:::

### Reading R Output

`TukeyHSD(model)` prints one row for each pair of treatments:

| Column | Meaning |
|:---|:---|
| `diff` | difference between the two sample means, in the order of the row name (e.g. `Discount-Regular` = $\bar{x}_D - \bar{x}_R$) |
| `lwr`, `upr` | lower and upper limits of a 95% (family-wise) CI for the difference |
| `p adj` | adjusted p-value for $H_0: \mu_i = \mu_j$ |

A pair is significantly different if `p adj` $< 0.05$; equivalently, if the CI
from `lwr` to `upr` **does not contain 0**.

```{r}
#| label: ex-4-2
tk <- TukeyHSD(model)$strategy
mns <- tapply(crd$sales, crd$strategy, mean)
```

### Example

**Example 4.2.1.** In Example 4.1.1 the ANOVA rejected $H_0$
(p-value = `r fmt(summary(model)[[1]][1, "Pr(>F)"], 4)`). The sample means are
Regular `r num(mns[1])`, Discount `r num(mns[2])` and Bundle `r num(mns[3])`.
Use the Tukey output to find which pricing strategies differ at $\alpha$ = 0.05.

```{r}
#| label: r-tukey-crd
#| echo: !expr show_code
model <- aov(sales ~ strategy)    # data of Example 4.1.1
TukeyHSD(model)
```

::: {.callout-tip icon=false collapse=false}
## Solution

| Pair | diff | 95% CI | p adj | Decision |
|:---|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---|
| Discount $-$ Regular | `r num(tk[1, "diff"])` | (`r fmt(tk[1, "lwr"], 4)`, `r fmt(tk[1, "upr"], 4)`) | `r fmt(tk[1, "p adj"], 4)` | < 0.05: different |
| Bundle $-$ Regular | `r num(tk[2, "diff"])` | (`r fmt(tk[2, "lwr"], 4)`, `r fmt(tk[2, "upr"], 4)`) | `r fmt(tk[2, "p adj"], 4)` | < 0.05: different |
| Bundle $-$ Discount | `r num(tk[3, "diff"])` | (`r fmt(tk[3, "lwr"], 4)`, `r fmt(tk[3, "upr"], 4)`) | `r fmt(tk[3, "p adj"], 4)` | $\ge$ 0.05: not different |

At the 0.05 level of significance:

- mean sales with the Discount strategy are higher than with the Regular strategy;
- mean sales with the Bundle strategy are higher than with the Regular strategy;
- mean sales with the Discount and Bundle strategies are equal.

Both promotional strategies beat the regular price, but there is no significant
difference between them.
:::

```{r}
#| label: yt-4-2
ts <- TukeyHSD(model_sav)$region
```

### Your Turn

::: {.callout-note icon=false}
## Your Turn 4.2.1

In Your Turn 4.1.1 the ANOVA showed that the mean saving rates differ among the
four regions. Use the output below to decide which pairs of regions differ at
$\alpha$ = 0.05, and summarize the result in one or two sentences.
:::

```{r}
#| label: r-tukey-sav
#| echo: !expr show_code
model_sav <- aov(saving ~ region)    # data of Your Turn 4.1.1
TukeyHSD(model_sav)
```

::: {.workspace lines="12"}
:::

::: {.answer title="Your Turn 4.2.1"}
Pairs with p adj < 0.05 (CI does not contain 0):
`r paste(sprintf("%s (p adj = %s)", gsub("-", " $-$ ", rownames(ts)[ts[, "p adj"] < 0.05]), fmt(ts[ts[, "p adj"] < 0.05, "p adj"], 4)), collapse = "; ")`.
All other pairs are not significantly different.

That is, at the 0.05 level of significance the mean saving rate in the
Northeast is lower than in the North and lower than in the Central region; the
other pairs of regions have equal mean saving rates.
:::

### Formula Summary

| | |
|:---|:---|
| When | after ANOVA rejects $H_0$ |
| R | `TukeyHSD(model)` (CRD); `TukeyHSD(model, "trt")` (RCBD, Section 4.3) |
| Decision for a pair | different if `p adj` < 0.05, equivalently if (`lwr`, `upr`) does not contain 0 |
| Direction | sign of `diff` (row `A-B` means $\bar{x}_A - \bar{x}_B$) |

### Exercises

**4.2.1** A Tukey output for three loan products contains the row

```
                diff       lwr       upr     p adj
Car-Personal  -1.85  -3.12000  -0.58000 0.0041000
```

Interpret this row.

::: {.answer title="Exercise 4.2.1"}
The mean for car loans is 1.85 lower than for personal loans
($\bar{x}_{\text{Car}} - \bar{x}_{\text{Personal}} = -1.85$). The 95% CI
(-3.12, -0.58) does not contain 0 and p adj = 0.0041 < 0.05, so the mean
for car loans is lower than for personal loans at the 0.05 level of significance.
:::

**4.2.2** An ANOVA comparing four advertising channels gives p-value = 0.2840. A
student then runs `TukeyHSD()` and finds one pair with p adj = 0.0470. What
should the conclusion be?

::: {.answer title="Exercise 4.2.2"}
The ANOVA accepts $H_0$ (0.2840 $\ge$ 0.05), so the conclusion is that the mean
outcomes of the four channels are equal. Tukey's method should not be used
after ANOVA accepts $H_0$.
:::
